sentiment.instructions: Judge the overall sentiment the author expresses or the text conveys: the emotional tone toward the events, people, or things mentioned. Consider sarcasm, complaints, excitement, and implied attitudes, not just keywords. Applies to texts in any language.

criteria.positive: Text conveys happiness, excitement, anticipation, praise, pride, enthusiasm, or good news (e.g., promoting a fun upcoming event, celebrating a win or achievement, loving a film, looking forward to something, favorable outcomes even if phrased jokingly or as mockery of a rival).
criteria.neutral: Text is mainly informational, factual, logistical, or a question/announcement without clear emotional stance (news headlines, schedules, plans, sales, scores, weather), or contains mixed or very mild feelings that don't tip clearly either way, including light sarcasm without real complaint.
criteria.negative: Text conveys frustration, disappointment, anger, sadness, insult, criticism, fear, or reports harmful events (violence, terrorism, injuries, cancellations, losses, bigotry). Includes complaints, mocking or derisive remarks, sarcasm aimed at criticizing, dark jokes, and worried or pessimistic predictions.
